title: Geometric node completion gives the Fitting and depth conditions
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $R$ a finitely generated $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $\mathfrak q\subset R$ a maximal ideal such that $R/\mathfrak q=K$ via the structure map. Put $B=R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qB$, and $J_B=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{R/K})B$, where $\Omega$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\operatorname{Fit}_1$ is the presentation-minor ideal of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] with index $1$. Write $\widehat B$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If $\widehat B$ is isomorphic as a ring, without requiring $K$-linearity, to $K[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], then $J_B=\mathfrak n$ and $\operatorname{depth}B=\operatorname{depth}\widehat B=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal), algebraically closed case, and 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), using 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic); completion contraction and depth comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] with $k=K$, $S=R$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q$ and $F=K$; the identity extension $K/K$ is finite separable. Thus $B$ and $\widehat B$ are Noetherian local rings, the maximal ideal of $\widehat B$ is $\mathfrak n\widehat B$, and its residue field is $K$. The given ring isomorphism is not assumed $K$-linear. Apply [lem-trf-rational-nodal-completion-algebra] with these same data to obtain instead a continuous surjective $K$-algebra map $\pi:K[[u,v]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat B$ with kernel $(uv)$ and with the prescribed structure map on constants. Write $x=\pi(u)$, $y=\pi(v)$. Then $(x,y)=\mathfrak n\widehat B$.

source.place: Tags 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic) and 0C4D (lemma-nodal), algebraically closed case; coefficient-compatible presentation from varieties.tex Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra).

proof.text: The module $\Omega_{R/K}$ is finite: if $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ generate $R$ as a $K$-algebra, the additive and Leibniz relations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] express the differential of each polynomial in them as an $R$-linear combination of $\mathrm dr_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{B/K}\cong\Omega_{R/K}\otimes_R B$. Applying the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] first to $R\to B$, then to $B\to\widehat B$, gives $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{B/K})=J_B$ and $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{B/K}\otimes_B\widehat B)=J_B\widehat B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), polynomial differential presentation; algebra.tex Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize); more-algebra.tex Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics)(3).

proof.text: Use the presentation $\pi$ of step 1 and the $K$-algebra section $K\to\widehat B$ given by the structure map. Its composite with the residue map is the identity by the rationality hypothesis. The completed-Jacobian statement [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials], with $n=2$, $s=1$, $f_1=uv$, identifies $\Omega_{B/K}\otimes_B\widehat B$ with the cokernel of $\widehat B\to\widehat B^{\oplus2}$ having column $(y,x)^{\mathsf T}$. The index-$1$ ideal in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] is therefore the ideal of its $1\times1$ minors, namely $(y,x)$. Indeed the kernel of the surjection from $\widehat B^{\oplus2}$ is generated by this column, so all its row entries generate exactly $(y,x)$. Step 2 now gives $J_B\widehat B=(x,y)=\mathfrak n\widehat B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof of (1) implies (3), and Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), completed Jacobian calculation.

proof.text: Since $B$ is Noetherian local, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] applies to $B\to\widehat B$. Contract the equality of extended ideals in step 3 along this map. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], the inverse images of $J_B\widehat B$ and $\mathfrak n\widehat B$ are respectively $J_B$ and $\mathfrak n$. Hence $J_B=\mathfrak n$.

Apply [lem-trf-binary-quadratic-model-depth] to $Q=uv$ (coefficients $a=c=0$, $b=1$). It gives depth $1$ for $K[[u,v]]/(uv)$, hence depth $1$ for $\widehat B$: the isomorphism in step 1 bijects maximal ideals and regular sequences, preserving multiplication injectivity and nonzero successive quotients as defined in [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and [def-weil-pbc-depth]. The completion map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] and is local because its extended maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n\widehat B$, the maximal ideal from step 1. Both rings are Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] gives $\operatorname{depth}\widehat B=\operatorname{depth}B+\operatorname{depth}(\widehat B/\mathfrak n\widehat B)$. The closed fibre is the nonzero field $K$. Its depth is zero: its maximal ideal is zero, and multiplication by zero on $K$ is not injective, so only the empty regular sequence occurs. Thus $1=\operatorname{depth}\widehat B=\operatorname{depth}B$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q28-3ea24f166 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole item, every cited node's statement, and Stacks curves.tex 0C49, 0C4C and 0C4D (algebraically closed case). The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are unchanged from the unsplit version in the Q95 parent snapshot. No new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; no cycle; no SGA citation. Step 1: the separable-closed-point presentation with F=K (identity extension K/K, finite separable) gives B and B̂ Noetherian local, maximal ideal nB̂, residue field K. The rational-nodal-completion node (unsplit, hypotheses match exactly, and I checked it is true via Cohen's theorem plus the intrinsic graded ring K[u,v]/(uv)) gives a K-linear π: K[[u,v]]→B̂ with kernel (uv), so (x,y)=nB̂. Step 2: Ω_{R/K} is finitely generated; Ω localizes; Fitting clause (2) for an arbitrary ring map applies along R→B and B→B̂. Step 3: the completed-Jacobian node with n=2, s=1, f=uv and σ the structure map gives coker of the column (y,x); the index-1 Fitting ideal (1×1 minors) is (x,y), with no characteristic-2 issue. Step 4: completion is faithfully flat and extended ideals contract back, so J_B=n. Step 5: the binary-quadratic depth node with b=1 gives depth 1 for K[[u,v]]/(uv), and depth carries over along the abstract ring isomorphism. The flat-local depth formula then applies (flat, local, Noetherian), the closed fibre K has depth 0, so depth B=1. Duplicates checked: the closest, lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion, offers an alternative route, not a duplicate. lean.statement: theorem geometricNode_fitting_depth (K : Type u) (R : Type v) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [CommRing R] [Algebra K R] [Algebra.FiniteType K R] (q : Ideal R) [q.IsMaximal] (hrational : Function.Bijective (algebraMap K (R ⧸ q))) (hnode : Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Localization.AtPrime q) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) K ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.X (0 : Fin 2) * MvPowerSeries.X (1 : Fin 2)} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) K))))) : (∀ (n : ℕ) (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] KaehlerDifferential K R), Function.Surjective π → Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) (π.presentationFittingIdeal 1) = Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q)) q) ∧ IsLocalRing.depth (R := Localization.AtPrime q) (Localization.AtPrime q) = 1 ∧ (Ideal.map (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime q) (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Localization.AtPrime q))) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))).depth (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Localization.AtPrime q)) = 1
lean.note: The index-one Fitting ideal is expressed for every finite generating surjection using the recorded presentationFittingIdeal. The completed depth uses Ideal.depth at the extended maximal ideal, which is the maximal ideal of the completion; this is exactly local-ring depth.
